Everything here is optional and configured in Admin → System settings; Admin → Chat channels shows whether each bot is connected.

docs.title: Chat platforms
docs.text:
Platform How SlotServe receives messages Public URL needed Buttons Telegram Long polling No Inline buttons Feishu / Lark Long connection (WebSocket) No Interactive cards DingTalk Stream mode (WebSocket) No Numbered choices (tap to send) WeCom Callback URL Only to receive commands Numbered choices QQ WebSocket gateway No Numbered choices

Every platform offers the same commands and notifications. Turn on as many as you like: a person gets each notification on every platform they linked, and which notifications they get is chosen once for all platforms.

Linking. Each person opens Settings → Chat notifications and presses Link next to a platform. Telegram opens the bot and pressing Start links the account. On the other platforms SlotServe shows a message like bind K7P2QX; send it to the SlotServe bot in a private chat within 30 minutes (绑定 K7P2QX works too). A code works once; one platform account belongs to one SlotServe account. Send test checks the connection, the Notify switch pauses one platform, and Unlink (or /unlink in the chat) removes it.

Messages are sent in each person's interface language. Times use the Time zone setting. Group chats and people who have not linked yet get the Group chat language.

Notification Who gets it Booking starts in 10 minutes Booker Model loaded and ready / GPU free for an exclusive booking Booker Booking ends in 10 minutes, with +30 min, +1 hour and End now buttons Booker An admin booked, changed, cancelled or ended your booking Booker The booked model failed to load and the default model is serving instead Booker and admins Your booking request was approved, rejected (with the reason) or expired Booker Your dev environment is ready (with the ssh command) or could not start Booker Time you waited for is free, or was booked for you Waitlisted person Your download finished or failed Person who started it A booking needs approval, with Approve and Reject buttons Admins A model failed to load, a new account was created, the models disk is low Admins

Commands (private chat with the bot):

Command What it does /status Loaded model and who has the GPU /book Book GPU time with buttons: lane, model (or whole GPU), day, start, length, confirm /free Free time today and tomorrow, per lane /cancel Pick one of your upcoming bookings and cancel it /today Bookings in the next 24 hours /mine Your upcoming bookings /extend [minutes] Extend your running booking (default 30) /release End your running booking now /unlink Stop notifications to this chat

Bookings made with /book follow exactly the same rules as the web: conflicts, the longest booking, how far ahead, quotas and approval. The bot offers whole-hour start times (and Now); use the web for other times, presets or weekly repeats. If the time is taken by the moment you confirm, the bot offers to put you on the waitlist.

Outside Telegram, commands also work without the / and in Chinese (状态, 预约, 空闲, 取消, 今天, 我的, 延长, 结束, 解绑). Where a platform has no buttons, the choices are numbered and you reply with the number; on DingTalk the numbers are links that send themselves. In a group chat (not on Telegram) the bot only answers /status, /free, /today and /help when it is @mentioned; everything that touches one person's bookings works in the private chat.

docs.title: Telegram
docs.text:
The bot uses long polling, so the server needs outbound access to Telegram but no public address or open port.

  1. In Telegram, talk to @BotFather, send /newbot and copy the token.
  2. Paste it into Admin → System settings → Telegram bot token and save. If Telegram is blocked on your network, also set Telegram proxy (http://… or socks5://…).
  3. People link with Settings → Chat notifications → Link next to Telegram. Typing / in Telegram shows the command list.

docs.title: Feishu / Lark
docs.text:
A self-built app with the bot ability. Events and card button presses arrive over the long connection that SlotServe opens, so no public address is needed.

  1. In the developer console (open.feishu.cn/app, for Lark open.larksuite.com/app) create a custom app (self-built app) and add the Bot ability.
  2. Under Permissions & Scopes add: read and send messages in private and group chats (im:message), send messages as the app (im:message:send_as_bot), receive private messages (im:message.p2p_msg:readonly) and receive group messages that mention the bot (im:message.group_at_msg:readonly).
  3. Copy App ID and App Secret from Credentials & Basic Info into Admin → System settings → Feishu / Lark bot, switch it on and save. For Lark set Open platform address to https://open.larksuite.com. Wait until Admin → Chat channels shows Connected.
  4. Under Events & Callbacks, choose Receive events through persistent connection for both events and callbacks (the console only saves this while SlotServe is connected), then add the event im.message.receive_v1 (Receive messages) and the callback card.action.trigger (Card action).
  5. Create a version, include the people who should use the bot in its availability, and publish it.

docs.title: DingTalk
docs.text:
An internal app robot in Stream mode: SlotServe opens a WebSocket to DingTalk, so no public address is needed.

  1. In the developer console create an internal app (H5 micro app or app with a robot) and add the Robot capability. Set the robot's message receiving mode to Stream mode.
  2. Under Permissions make sure the app may send robot messages to people in the organisation (qyapi_robot_sendmsg), which notifications need.
  3. Copy Client ID (AppKey) and Client Secret (AppSecret) from Credentials & Basic Info into Admin → System settings → DingTalk bot, switch it on and save. Robot code can stay empty: it defaults to the Client ID, as for most internal apps.
  4. Publish the app version with the right visibility. People find the robot by name (or open it from the app) and send their bind message. In a group, add the robot to the group and @mention it.

DingTalk robot messages cannot carry callback buttons without a card template, so choices are numbered; the numbers are links that send themselves back to the robot.

docs.title: WeCom
docs.text:
A self-built app. Sending uses WeCom's server API and needs no public address. Receiving commands, including the bind message, needs WeCom to reach SlotServe's callback URL over the internet.

  1. In the WeCom admin console create a self-built app under App Management. Note its AgentId and Secret, and set its visibility to the people who should use it.
  2. Copy the Corp ID from My Enterprise → Enterprise Information.
  3. In the app's settings add the SlotServe server's public outbound IP under Trusted IP (required for newer apps calling the API).
  4. To receive messages, open the app's Receive messages → Set API receiving, generate a Token and an EncodingAESKey, and keep the page open.
  5. Paste Corp ID, AgentId, Secret, Token and EncodingAESKey into Admin → System settings → WeCom app, switch it on and save.
  6. Back in WeCom, enter the callback URL shown in Admin → Chat channels (https://<your server>/api/channels/wecom/callback) and save; WeCom checks it right away. WeCom may require the URL's domain to be a domain verified for your organisation.

Without the callback (step 4–6) the WeCom bot cannot receive the bind message, so people cannot link it; group webhooks (below) still work.

docs.title: QQ
docs.text:
An official bot from the QQ open platform. SlotServe connects to QQ's WebSocket gateway and receives private (C2C) messages and group messages that @mention the bot.

  1. Create a bot on the QQ open platform and copy AppID and AppSecret from Development → Development settings.
  2. Add the SlotServe server's public outbound IP to the bot's IP whitelist.
  3. Make sure the bot may be used in private chats and groups (message capabilities for single chat and group). While the bot is not published, add test users and groups in the sandbox configuration and switch on Sandbox in SlotServe.
  4. Paste AppID and AppSecret into Admin → System settings → QQ bot, switch it on and save.

QQ only lets bots reply to a message for a limited time; answers to commands use that. Notifications are proactive messages, which QQ limits or refuses depending on the bot's permissions, so on QQ they may not arrive. QQ may also block links in messages unless the domain is registered with the bot.

docs.title: Group webhooks
docs.text:
Group robots post into a group chat. They only send, need no public address, and are configured under Admin → System settings → Group webhooks:

  • Feishu / Lark: in the group, Settings → Bots → Add Bot → Custom Bot. Copy the webhook (https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v2/hook/…). If you turn on Signature verification, also paste its secret.
  • DingTalk: in the group, Group settings → Bots → Add Robot → Custom. Choose the security setting Additional signature and paste its SEC… secret together with the webhook (https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=…). (Keyword security would reject most SlotServe messages.)
  • WeCom: in the group chat, Add group robot, then copy its webhook (https://qyapi.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/webhook/send?key=…). Its key is in the URL.

Send to groups chooses what the groups get: Admin alerts (load failures and fallbacks, new accounts, low disk), Approval requests (as text; approve on the web or in a private chat with the bot) and Announcements. Admin → Chat channels has a Send test button per webhook and a box to post an announcement.

docs.title: Calendar subscription
docs.text:
Settings → Calendar subscription shows two private iCalendar links: your own bookings, and everyone's. Add them as a subscribed or internet calendar in Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook or Thunderbird. Calendar apps refresh them periodically (usually every 15 minutes to a few hours).

Anyone with a link can read the bookings in it. New link invalidates the old ones. Set Public URL if people reach SlotServe through an address different from the one the browser shows.

docs.title: CSV export
docs.text:
Usage → Export CSV downloads, for the selected period and scope (everyone or just you):

Export Columns Per person person, bookings, booked hours, booked GPU-hours, used GPU-hours, average utilization % while booked, peak memory (MB), energy (Wh), requests, prompt and completion tokens GPU time date, lane, GPU, kind, person, GPU-hours, used GPU-hours, average utilization %, peak memory (MB), energy (Wh); one row per day, lane, GPU, kind and person Daily summary date, person, model, requests, prompt and completion tokens Every request time, person, API key, model, endpoint, stream, status, tokens, duration

Kinds are model, gpu (whole-GPU booking), devenv, idle_model and idle_devenv (shared use while nobody books the lane) and free. The GPU column is empty for a lane without GPU metrics. The same files are available at GET /api/usage/export?kind=people|compute|summary|requests&days=30&scope=all|mine. Files are UTF-8 with a BOM so Excel opens them correctly.

docs.title: Prometheus
docs.text:
Set Metrics token to enable GET /metrics. Scrape it with the token as a bearer token:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: slotserve
    metrics_path: /metrics
    authorization:
      credentials: <metrics token>
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["gpu-server:8000"]
Metric Type Labels slotserve_runtime_state gauge state slotserve_runtime_model_info gauge model, preset slotserve_reservation_active gauge user slotserve_reservations_upcoming gauge slotserve_requests_total counter user, model, outcome (ok / error) slotserve_tokens_total counter user, model, type slotserve_request_seconds_total counter user, model slotserve_model_loads_total counter model, result slotserve_model_load_seconds gauge model slotserve_downloads_pending gauge slotserve_gpu_memory_used_bytes, …_total_bytes, slotserve_gpu_utilization_ratio, slotserve_gpu_temperature_celsius, slotserve_gpu_power_watts gauge gpu, name, lane slotserve_lane_occupant gauge lane, kind, user (what the lane is doing now) slotserve_booked_gpu_hours_total counter user, lane, kind (elapsed booked time × GPUs of the lane) slotserve_gpu_seconds_total counter lane, gpu, kind (recorded GPU time) slotserve_gpu_busy_seconds_total counter lane, gpu, kind (time at or above the busy threshold) slotserve_gpu_energy_joules_total counter lane, gpu slotserve_user_gpu_busy_seconds_total counter user, kind

Without a token the endpoint returns 404.

docs.title: Model catalog
docs.text: Models → Catalog lists popular open models that run well on a single server, with one-click deployment. Every file in the built-in catalog was checked against the Hugging Face API, and the sizes shown are exact.

docs.title: What is in it
docs.text:
About 35 models in five groups, most of them in several sizes:

Task Examples Chat / instruct Qwen3 (4B–32B, 30B-A3B), Llama 3.1 8B / 3.2 3B, Gemma 3 (4B, 12B, 27B), Mistral Small 3.2, Phi-4, gpt-oss 20B / 120B Coding Qwen2.5 Coder (7B, 14B, 32B), Qwen3 Coder 30B-A3B, Devstral Small Reasoning DeepSeek R1 distills (7B, 14B, 32B, Qwen3 8B), QwQ 32B, Qwen3, Phi-4, gpt-oss Embeddings Qwen3 Embedding (0.6B, 4B, 8B), Nomic Embed Text v1.5, BGE-M3 Vision-language Qwen2.5 VL (3B, 7B, 32B), Qwen3 VL (4B, 8B, 30B-A3B), Gemma 3, Mistral Small 3.2

Each entry shows its publisher, licence, parameters (total and active for mixture-of-experts models), maximum context and a short description, plus one or more variants:

  • GGUF for llama.cpp: a quantization (Q4_K_M, Q8_0, ...), the exact files including split parts, and the vision projector (mmproj) for vision models.
  • safetensors for vLLM or SGLang: the original weights or an FP8 / AWQ / MXFP4 checkpoint. Only the files an engine needs are downloaded (config, tokenizer, weights) - not original checkpoints, other runtimes' formats or images.

Variants marked Licence required come from gated repositories: accept the licence on the model's Hugging Face page and set a Hugging Face token in Admin → System settings before deploying them. Most popular gated models also have ungated GGUF variants.

Filter by task, size, engine and fits on lane, or search names, publishers, tags and quantizations.

docs.title: Will it fit?
docs.text:
For every variant the catalog estimates the GPU memory needed to serve one request:

  • weights: the download size (plus the vision projector),
  • KV cache for the context: 2 × layers × KV heads × head size × context × 2 bytes (16-bit cache; an upper bound for models with sliding-window layers),
  • overhead: about 0.5 GB + 3 % of the weights for llama.cpp, about 1.5 GB + 5 % for vLLM / SGLang (activations, CUDA graphs).

The estimate is compared with the total memory of each lane's GPUs, as reported by nvidia-smi:

Badge Meaning fits Below 95 % of the lane's memory (90 % for vLLM / SGLang, which reserve a fixed share). tight Fits only just: use a shorter context or offload fewer layers. too large Needs more memory than the lane has. llama.cpp can still run it partly on the CPU, slowly. unknown No GPU information for the lane (no NVIDIA driver, or the lane's GPUs are not detected).

Cards show, per lane, the largest variant that fits. Change the context in the deploy dialog to see how the KV cache grows; parallel requests (--parallel / -np) need more.

docs.title: Deploying
docs.text:
Press Deploy on a card or on a variant in Details, then choose:

  • the variant and, for safetensors, the engine (vLLM or SGLang),
  • the context length (default 8K tokens, less when the model supports less),
  • the lane (used for the fit check and, for vLLM / SGLang on lanes with several GPUs, tensor parallelism),
  • optionally a model name (default <entry>-<variant>, for example qwen3-8b-q4_k_m),
  • (admins) make it the default model on that lane.

SlotServe then queues the files in the normal download queue - so the configured Hugging Face endpoint and token are used, downloads resume after interruptions and appear under Downloads - after checking that the disk has room for all of them plus Keep free after downloads. GGUF files go into the models folder as with the Hugging Face tab; safetensors repositories go into a folder named <org>--<repo>. The catalog shows the progress of each deployment, and when the last file arrives the model is registered with default launch arguments:

Engine Arguments llama.cpp -ngl 99 -c <context>, plus --mmproj <file> for vision models and --embedding --pooling ... for embedding models vLLM --max-model-len <context>, plus --tensor-parallel-size <GPUs> on multi-GPU lanes and --runner pooling for embedding models SGLang --context-length <context>, plus --tp-size <GPUs> on multi-GPU lanes and --is-embedding for embedding models

Some entries add more (for example --jinja for gpt-oss and the Mistral tokenizer options). Everything can be edited afterwards like any other model, and presets work as usual. Arguments for engine flags change between engine versions; if a model fails to start, check Server log.

Deploying something that is already there does not download again: if the files are on disk the model is registered right away, and if it is registered already it is simply reused (and made the lane default if asked). If a download fails, retry it in Downloads; the deployment continues when every file has arrived. Removing a deployment from the catalog's list cancels its queued downloads.

docs.title: Managing the catalog (admins)
docs.text:
• Hide a built-in entry in its Details to remove it from everyone's catalog; Show hidden brings it back.
  • Add entry creates your own entry: name, tasks, parameters, context, descriptions, and variants given as a Hugging Face repository plus (for GGUF) a file name - the first part of split files is enough. SlotServe looks up the file sizes and split parts on Hugging Face, and reads config.json of the original repository for the KV-cache estimate. Your entries can be edited and deleted; deleting one keeps installed models.

The built-in list lives in backend/slotserve/resources/model_catalog.json. To refresh it after editing (or to check it is still accurate), run from the repository root:

PYTHONPATH=backend python tools/update_model_catalog.py          # verify and rewrite sizes
PYTHONPATH=backend python tools/update_model_catalog.py --check  # report only

It fails on any repository or file that no longer exists. Set HF_TOKEN to read gated repositories and HF_ENDPOINT to use a mirror.

docs.title: API
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/catalog?ctx= Entries with estimates and fit per lane (ctx overrides the context of every estimate) GET /api/catalog/{entry}?ctx= One entry POST /api/catalog/deploy {entry_id, variant_id, engine?, lane_id?, set_default?, ctx?, name?} GET / DELETE /api/catalog/deploys, /api/catalog/deploys/{id} Recent deployments with progress; remove (cancel) one PUT /api/catalog/{entry}/hidden Admin: {hidden} POST / PUT / DELETE /api/catalog/entries, /api/catalog/entries/{entry} Admin: own entries

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Runbooks for the people who keep a SlotServe installation running: upgrading, backups and restore, the first admin, reverse proxies, health checks and alerts, container hardening, firewall ports and checking an installation on real hardware. Each problem runbook reads symptom → diagnose → fix → prevent.

The commands assume the Docker Compose installation from Getting started, run in the folder with docker-compose.yml. Without Docker, drop the docker compose exec slotserve prefix and run slotserve ... as the user that runs SlotServe, with the same environment (.env).

Situation Go to Moving from v0.8 to v0.10 Upgrade from v0.8 An upgrade went wrong Upgrade failed: roll back Setting up or checking backups Backups, The secret key Putting a backup back, moving to another machine Restore from a backup, Move to a new machine Nobody can sign in as admin First admin and setup code, Forgotten admin password Running behind nginx, Caddy or Traefik Reverse proxy Something is red on Admin → Overview Health checks and slotserve doctor, Inbox and alerts sudo or an app does not work in an environment Container hardening and compatibility mode Which ports to open Ports and firewall Disk full, GPUs gone, environments do not start, a leaked password Runbooks Checking an installation before people use it Verify on real hardware

docs.title: Upgrade from v0.8
docs.text: v0.10 changes how people sign in, how dev environments are isolated and how data is backed up. Most of it needs nothing from you; this section lists what people will notice and what to check. The full list is under Breaking changes in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Before you upgrade
docs.text:
1. Read the Breaking changes of the release.
  2. Make a backup you can find again: Admin → Overview → Backups → Back up now, or stop SlotServe and copy the whole data directory (DATA_DIR, default ./data). The upgrade also takes its own snapshot (below).
  3. Note your image tag. docker-compose.yml now follows a minor version (ghcr.io/peleryuan/slotserve:0.10, which gets 0.10.x fixes) instead of latest. If your .env sets SLOTSERVE_IMAGE, change it to the new version.
  4. Tell people about the one-time sign-in and the SSH host key warning below. Running dev environments keep running while SlotServe restarts; the new container settings apply on their next start.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
git pull                      # the new docker-compose.yml and docs
docker compose pull           # or: docker compose up -d --build
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f slotserve

On the first start the server:

  • saves a snapshot before it changes the database: data/backups/slotserve-v<old>-to-v<new>-<time>/ with the database, secret_key and the dev environment SSH host keys. Snapshots are never deleted automatically;
  • applies the numbered database migrations all or nothing (a failure rolls back and the server does not start; see Roll back) and writes data/migration_report.json;
  • generates a secret key in data/secret_key if SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY is unset or still change-me (see The secret key).

reset-password and set-admin refuse to run on a database that still needs upgrading: start the server once first.

docs.title: What people notice
docs.text:
Everyone signs in once more. Browser sign-ins are now stored on the server, so all old sign-ins end with the upgrade. API keys keep working unchanged. Changing your password now signs out your other browsers.

SSH warns about a changed host key, once per environment. Every dev environment now has its own SSH host key (before, all environments shared one that anyone could read inside their container). Existing environments get their key on their next start, and the first ssh afterwards stops with REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED. That is expected exactly once. Tell people to:

  1. compare the fingerprint ssh prints with the Host key shown on the environment's card (Dev environments);

  2. remove the old entry and connect again:

    ssh-keygen -R "[server]:2201"     # the host and port of the environment's ssh command

A warning after that first time, for an environment whose key has not changed on its card, is a real warning: do not ignore it. Kept environments created by an older version are snapshotted and recreated once on their next start (that start takes longer), because the new settings cannot be added to an existing container.

Shared environments of idle lanes need Join. They accept SSH keys only, and only people who joined them get an account (Dev environments → Join). Everyone who had an SSH key at the upgrade was joined to every lane.

Containers are hardened. sudo and other setuid programs stop working inside dev environments, ping does not work, and a fork bomb or out-of-memory job stays inside its container. A memory limit of 0 now means "the host's memory less max(4 GB, 10 %)" instead of "no limit". A lane that names no GPUs cannot start a GPU environment any more: give the lane its GPUs in Admin → GPUs & lanes. Templates that really need sudo or their own init system run in compatibility mode; see Container hardening.

Sign-ups. Installations that already have an admin are not asked for a setup code. While the invite code is still change-me, nobody can sign up: set an invite code or hand out invite links (Admin → Users).

Behind a reverse proxy, changes in the web UI may be refused with "did not come from a SlotServe page" until the proxy passes the Host header or SLOTSERVE_PUBLIC_URL is set, and sign-in throttling needs SLOTSERVE_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS. See Reverse proxy.

Firewall. Dev environment web interfaces (VS Code, JupyterLab, the desktop) are served on their own port, 8001 by default. Open it if people use them; see Ports and firewall.

docs.title: Check the upgrade
docs.text:
1. Admin → Overview: the setup checklist and the system health table. Every check should be OK or a note you understand; see Health checks.
  2. docker compose exec slotserve slotserve doctor gives the same list on the command line.
  3. data/migration_report.json lists every migration step; the health check migration warns when an upgrade could not keep some rows.
  4. Sign in, open a dev environment in the browser, call a model in the Playground.

docs.title: Upgrade failed: roll back
docs.text:
Symptom. The server does not come up after an upgrade, or it runs but something you rely on is broken.

Diagnose.

  • docker compose logs slotserve shows why. A failed migration says database upgrade failed and was rolled back; the snapshot is in ...: the database is unchanged and still the old version's.
  • An older version started on an upgraded database refuses to start with ... was used by a newer SlotServe. This protects your data; it is not the problem itself.

Fix. To run the previous version again:

docker compose stop slotserve
ls -d data/backups/slotserve-v*-to-v*          # the newest is the snapshot of this upgrade
SNAP=data/backups/slotserve-v...-to-v...-<time>   # the folder name from ls
cp "$SNAP/slotserve.db" data/slotserve.db
rm -f data/slotserve.db-wal data/slotserve.db-shm
[ -f "$SNAP/secret_key" ] && cp "$SNAP/secret_key" data/secret_key
[ -d "$SNAP/devenv" ] && cp -r "$SNAP/devenv" data/

Then pin the old version in .env and start it:

echo "SLOTSERVE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/peleryuan/slotserve:0.8.0" >> .env
docker compose up -d

Everything that happened between the upgrade and the rollback (bookings, keys, settings) is lost with the newer database; keep data/slotserve.db somewhere before overwriting it if you may need it. When the migration itself failed (the database was not changed), only pinning the old version is needed.

Prevent. Rehearse the upgrade on a copy of the data directory first (another folder as DATA_DIR, another PORT, dev environments off). Keep the image pinned to a minor version and upgrade on purpose. Report a failed migration with data/migration_report.json and the log.

docs.title: What a backup contains
docs.text:
Every day at backup_hour (default 3:00 in the SlotServe time zone; -1 = every 24 hours from the last one) SlotServe writes a bundle, a folder data/backups/slotserve-daily-<date>-<time>/ with:

File What it is slotserve.db A consistent copy of the database (SQLite's online backup, safe while the server runs) secret_key The generated secret key; absent when the key comes from SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY devenv/ The dev environments' SSH host keys manifest.json Version, schema, the key's fingerprint (never the key), sizes, checksums, row counts, the storages and kept environments, and what the bundle does not contain

Admin → Overview → Backups lists the bundles, makes one on demand (Back up now, a manual bundle) and downloads the database file. The newest backup_keep (default 7) daily and manual bundles are kept; upgrade snapshots and prerestore bundles are never removed automatically. backup_keep 0 switches automatic backups off.

Not in a backup: /workspace and other kept directories, kept environments' containers, saved environment images, models, and the data on managed storages. Back those up separately where they live:

  • Storages (Admin → Storage: host folders, NFS, SMB): with the backup of that server or folder.

  • Docker volumes (when no storage and no storage directory is set), e.g. one person's /workspace:

    docker run --rm -v slotserve-workspace-u3:/v:ro -v "$PWD":/out busybox:1.37 \
  tar czf /out/workspace-u3.tgz -C /v .

  • Models: usually downloaded again, or copied with the models folder.

  • Saved images: docker save the images you care about.

docs.title: Keep a copy off the machine
docs.text:
A backup on the same disk does not survive the disk. Set Copy backups to (backup_target, Admin → System settings) and every daily bundle is copied there after it is written, into a folder slotserve-backups/, keeping the newest backup_keep copies:

  • An absolute path SlotServe can write, typically a mounted NAS share. With Docker this is a path inside the container: mount the share into it first, e.g. in docker-compose.yml under volumes:

    - /mnt/nas/slotserve:/backup-target

    and set backup_target to /backup-target. - storage:<id>: a storage from Admin → Storage (its id is in the list). SlotServe writes the bundle through a short-lived helper container, so the share does not need to be mounted into SlotServe.

The setup checklist item Backups kept elsewhere ticks once a bundle has been copied.

docs.title: When a backup fails
docs.text:
The health checks backup and backup_age watch the backups, and admins are alerted (inbox, then chat platforms) when:

  • the last backup failed (the evidence has the error; Try again makes a new one);
  • the copy to the backup target failed or the target is not valid;
  • the newest backup is older than 36 hours (the server was down, or the backup task is stuck).

A warning "Backups are only on this machine's disk" stays until a backup target is set (it can be dismissed with a reason). /metrics exports slotserve_backup_age_seconds for external monitoring.

docs.title: The secret key
docs.text:
The secret key signs browser sessions and encrypts the secrets SlotServe stores: storage passwords (SMB) and the viewable copies of API keys (when Let people view their API keys again is on). It does not protect the API keys themselves (they are stored as hashes) or passwords (also hashes).

  • When SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY is unset, empty or change-me, SlotServe generates a random key on the first start and keeps it in data/secret_key (readable by its owner only). Every backup bundle includes it.
  • When SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY is set to anything else, that value is used and is not written into backups: keep it with your other secrets (a password manager), next to the .env.

What to back up: the backup bundles (copied off the machine), plus .env and, if you set it, the secret key. Copying the whole data directory while SlotServe is stopped is also a complete backup of SlotServe's own state.

docs.title: Secret key lost or changed
docs.text:
Symptom. After a restart or a move everyone is signed out; the health check secrets says "N stored secret(s) cannot be decrypted with the current secret key"; SMB storages fail to mount; viewable API key copies cannot be shown.

Diagnose. The check's evidence lists what cannot be decrypted. slotserve doctor shows the same. Compare the key's fingerprint in a bundle's manifest.json (secret_key.fingerprint) between a bundle from before and one from after the change.

Fix.

  • Put the old key back if you have it: the secret_key file of a bundle from before the change (stop SlotServe, copy it to data/secret_key, start), or the old value of SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY in .env. An explicitly set SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY always wins over data/secret_key: remove it from .env if you want the file to be used.
  • Without the old key, enter the listed secrets again: the password of each SMB storage in Admin → Storage; viewable API key copies cannot be recovered (the keys themselves keep working; their owners can make new ones). People sign in again.

Rotating the key on purpose (it leaked): stop SlotServe, set a new SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY (openssl rand -hex 32) or delete data/secret_key to have a new one generated, start, then re-enter the secrets as above. Everyone is signed out.

Prevent. Keep backups off the machine; if you set the key yourself, store it outside the server.

docs.title: Restore from a backup
docs.text:
slotserve restore puts a bundle back. The server must be stopped.

docker compose stop slotserve
docker compose run --rm --no-deps slotserve slotserve restore slotserve-daily-20261020-030000
docker compose up -d
  • The argument is a bundle folder name in data/backups/ or a path the command can see (inside the container: put a bundle from the NAS into DATA_DIR/backups/ first).
  • It asks you to type restore (--yes skips the question). It refuses a backup from a newer SlotServe and one that fails SQLite's integrity check.
  • Before it replaces anything, the current state is saved as a slotserve-prerestore-<time> bundle, so a restore can itself be undone the same way.
  • It puts back the database, the secret key (--keep-key keeps the current one; secrets of the backup then cannot be decrypted) and the SSH host keys. A backup from an older version is upgraded on the next start, after its own snapshot. The command prints warnings you must act on, for example that SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY in .env overrides the restored key.

Older single-file backups (slotserve-daily-<time>.db) and upgrade snapshots can be restored the same way.

docs.title: The reconciliation report
docs.text:
The restored database describes the moment of the backup, while Docker and the disk have moved on. On the next start SlotServe compares them and shows the result as the health check restore on Admin → Overview (also in data/restore_report.json):

Finding Meaning What to do Environment missing The database expects a container that Docker does not have (removed after the backup, or a new machine) For a kept environment, its installed software is gone; its kept directories are not affected. End or delete it, and start it again from its template. Unknown container A SlotServe container the database does not know (created after the backup) Save what matters from it (docker cp, or let its owner copy files out), then remove it with docker rm -f <name>. Model file missing A model whose file is not where the database says Copy the file back, or scan the models folder and remove the stale entry. Storages Listed for a re-check Press Check for each in Admin → Storage.

Volumes and ports are not compared. When Docker is not reachable the check waits ("waiting for Docker to compare") and runs once Docker is back.

Until an admin dismisses the restore check, SlotServe removes nothing the database does not know (no cleanup of unknown containers, networks or volumes). Read the report, deal with each line, then Dismiss it with a reason; normal cleanup resumes.

docs.title: Move to a new machine
docs.text:
1. Install SlotServe on the new machine as in Getting started, with the same or a newer version, and copy .env (it holds SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY if you set one). Do not start it yet.

  2. Copy the newest bundle into the new DATA_DIR/backups/ and restore it:

    docker compose run --rm --no-deps slotserve slotserve restore --yes slotserve-daily-20261020-030000

  3. Copy what is not in the bundle: the models folder, Docker volumes or the storage directory with /workspace and kept directories, saved images (docker save / docker load). Storages on a NAS only need the new machine to reach them (NFS exports allow its address; nfs-common / cifs-utils installed).

  4. Start (docker compose up -d) and read the reconciliation report: environments of the old machine are listed as missing.
  5. Point people at the new address (SLOTSERVE_PUBLIC_URL, DNS). Everyone's SSH known_hosts entries change with the address; the host keys themselves came with the bundle.

docs.title: First admin and setup code
docs.text:
A new installation has no admin. Until one exists, SlotServe prints a one-time setup code in its log at every start; the sign-up form asks for it instead of the invite code, and that account becomes the admin:

docker compose logs slotserve | grep -A4 "No admin account"
docker compose exec slotserve slotserve setup-code

The code stops working as soon as an admin exists, and installations that already have an admin never ask for it. While the invite code is still change-me, nobody else can sign up: set Invite code in Admin → System settings, or create invite links in Admin → Users (they expire, count their sign-ups, can be revoked and can ask for an admin's approval; they never contain the invite code).

More admins: Admin → Users, or docker compose exec slotserve slotserve set-admin <username> (--revoke to remove). Keep at least two admins so one can help the other.

docs.title: Reverse proxy
docs.text:
Put SlotServe behind a reverse proxy for HTTPS or a nicer address. Three things matter.

1. The address: Host or SLOTSERVE_PUBLIC_URL. SlotServe refuses changing requests (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) from a browser unless their Origin is SlotServe's own address: the host the request was sent to (Host, or X-Forwarded-Host) or the origin of SLOTSERVE_PUBLIC_URL. A proxy that rewrites Host to 127.0.0.1:8000 makes every change in the web UI fail with "did not come from a SlotServe page". Pass the original host, and set SLOTSERVE_PUBLIC_URL to the address people type (it is also used in links SlotServe sends):

SLOTSERVE_PUBLIC_URL=https://gpu.example.org
SLOTSERVE_COOKIE_SECURE=true                 # cookies only over HTTPS

2. Client addresses: SLOTSERVE_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS. Sign-in throttling locks an account per address (account + IP), the audit log records addresses and API keys show where they were last used. SlotServe only believes X-Forwarded-For from the proxies listed in SLOTSERVE_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (default 127.0.0.1). With Docker, the proxy's connections arrive from Docker's bridge address (for example 172.18.0.1), not 127.0.0.1: sign in once, look at the address of your sign-in in Admin → Audit log, and if it is the proxy's rather than your own, put that address in:

SLOTSERVE_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=172.18.0.1     # comma separated; "*" only if port 8000 is reachable from the proxy alone

Without it, everybody shares the proxy's address and failed sign-ins from one person can slow down others.

3. Streaming and the second port. Turn off buffering so model answers stream, allow long requests, and pass WebSockets. Dev environment web interfaces use port 8001 and need an address of their own (they must stay a different origin from SlotServe): a second server block or a second host name, with SLOTSERVE_DEVENV_WEB_URL set to it.

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name gpu.example.org;
    # ssl_certificate ...;
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_buffering off;
        proxy_read_timeout 1h;
        client_max_body_size 0;
    }
}

server {
    listen 8443 ssl;                            # or another server_name on 443
    server_name gpu.example.org;
    # ssl_certificate ...;
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8001;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_buffering off;
        proxy_read_timeout 1h;
    }
}

SLOTSERVE_DEVENV_WEB_URL=https://gpu.example.org:8443

The OpenAI-compatible API (/v1) works through the same proxy; clients use https://gpu.example.org/v1. SSH and direct ports of dev environments do not go through the proxy (see Ports and firewall).

docs.title: Health checks and slotserve doctor
docs.text:
One set of checks feeds every view of SlotServe's health:

Where What Who Admin → Overview Setup checklist, then the System health table: every check with its evidence, buttons, a diagnosis for recognised errors, and dismissing with a reason Admins GET /healthz Shallow: the process answers (Docker's HEALTHCHECK uses it) Anyone GET /api/health Every check as JSON (checks[], status: ok / degraded / down); ?strict=true answers 503 while a check fails, for uptime monitors Admin session or the metrics token (Authorization: Bearer <SLOTSERVE_METRICS_TOKEN>) GET /metrics Prometheus: slotserve_check_status, slotserve_backup_age_seconds and the GPU and usage metrics Metrics token slotserve doctor The same checks from the command line Shell on the server 
docker compose exec slotserve slotserve doctor          # while the server runs
docker compose run --rm --no-deps slotserve slotserve doctor   # when it does not start
slotserve doctor --json                                 # machine-readable, secrets removed

doctor prints one line per check (ok, info, WARN, ERROR) with the evidence of warnings and errors, and exits with code 1 when a check is at level error. It runs in its own process, so checks of the running server's internals (lanes, background tasks) are only in the web UI and /api/health.

Check What it looks at When it is not OK database The database can be written Disk full or read-only, file permissions disk Free space where data and models live, and on storages Disk full engine The inference engine program exists Fix LLAMA_CPP_DIR / SLOTSERVE_LLAMA_SERVER_CMD; see Configuration lanes Every lane's model server A failed load, with its diagnosis; FAQ: diagnoses models At least one model, an idle default per lane Add a model, set a default (Admin → GPUs & lanes) gpu nvidia-smi sees GPUs GPUs gone docker Docker is reachable (dev environments on) Dev environments: Docker storage Every storage mounts and is writable Storage, the diagnosis on the check chat Chat platforms are connected Admin → Chat channels backup The last backup and its copy off the machine Backups backup_age The newest backup is younger than 36 hours When a backup fails restore A restore waits for its reconciliation The reconciliation report migration The last upgrade kept every row data/migration_report.json tasks Background tasks run and report back Restart SlotServe; report the evidence secrets Stored secrets can be decrypted Secret key lost security Number of admins; dev environments mean root on the host A note to read once invite The invite code is not change-me Set an invite code or use invite links

Some results are notes rather than problems (no chat platform on purpose, a machine without GPU): Dismiss… them with a reason. A dismissed check stays in the table, no longer counts as a problem, and the reason is in the audit log; it comes back on its own when its level changes.

docs.title: Inbox and alerts
docs.text:
Every notification goes into the in-app inbox first (the bell in the header) and then to the chat platforms the person linked. Members get the news about their own work (approvals, reminders, environments that are ready or failed). Admins also get the admin messages: approvals to give, sign-ups waiting, failed model loads, storages that stop working, sensitive settings changes, and the health alerts.

  • A check that reaches its alert level (an error, for some checks a warning, some only after a while) sends one alert to all admins, and one more when it recovers. There are no repeats, also not across restarts. Dismissed checks do not alert.
  • Group webhooks (Feishu / Lark, DingTalk, WeCom) can get admin alerts too: Admin → Chat channels.
  • Without any chat platform nothing is lost: the inbox has everything. The Admin menu item shows how many admin messages are unread.
  • For monitoring from outside, poll /api/health?strict=true or scrape /metrics (slotserve_check_status).

docs.title: Container hardening and compatibility mode
docs.text:
Every container SlotServe starts for a dev environment is hardened in one fixed last step:

  • no new privileges: setuid programs such as sudo cannot gain rights;
  • capabilities NET_RAW, MKNOD, SYS_CHROOT, AUDIT_WRITE and SETFCAP are dropped (ping does not work);
  • at most SLOTSERVE_DEVENV_PIDS_LIMIT processes (default 4096), so a fork bomb stays inside its container;
  • a memory limit (the Memory limit setting, or with 0 the host's memory less max(4 GB, 10 %)), so an out-of-memory job is killed inside its container instead of taking SlotServe down;
  • bounded logs, exactly the lane's GPUs, never privileged, never the host's network or process namespace, never the Docker socket.

People are root inside their container, so apt install works without sudo. What changes:

Symptom inside an environment Why What to do sudo: effective uid is not 0 or a setuid program fails No new privileges Run as root without sudo. For an image that must use setuid (its own init system, a user switch), an admin turns on Compatibility mode in that template's settings (Dev environments, admins only; the built-in desktop already uses it). Less isolated: only for images you trust. ping: permission denied NET_RAW is dropped Use curl or nc to test connections. fork: Resource temporarily unavailable The process limit Fewer parallel workers, or raise SLOTSERVE_DEVENV_PIDS_LIMIT. A job is Killed The memory limit A smaller batch, or a higher Memory limit. Admins see the limit that applies in /api/devenv (hardening).

Web interface compatibility mode (Admin → System settings, SLOTSERVE_DEVENV_WEB_COMPAT) is a different switch: it relaxes the rules that keep the pages of one environment from acting in another one opened in the same browser (on the web port 8001). Turn it on only when an app in an environment's web interface does not work and nothing else helps; it weakens the isolation between environments and nothing else.

docs.title: Ports and firewall
docs.text:
Port What Who needs to reach it 8000 (PORT) Web UI, /api, the OpenAI-compatible /v1, /metrics Everyone (or only the reverse proxy) 8001 (DEVENV_WEB_PORT, SLOTSERVE_DEVENV_WEB_PORT) Dev environment web interfaces (VS Code, JupyterLab, desktop, your own web apps) Everyone who uses them (or only the reverse proxy) 8002 (SLOTSERVE_DEVENV_GATEWAY_PORT) The container-side gateway: only /v1, for code inside dev environments Only the dev environment containers; never open it to the network 2200-2299 (SSH ports) SSH into dev environments, one port per running environment Everyone who uses SSH 2300-2399 (Direct port range) Ports people publish directly from their environments Everyone who uses them; a direct port has no SlotServe login
  • The ranges are settings (SSH ports, Direct port range); keep them apart from each other and from ports the host uses.

  • Docker publishes the SSH and direct ports itself, through its own iptables rules, which bypass ufw and firewalld rules on the host. To restrict who can reach them, use the DOCKER-USER chain or a firewall in front of the machine, for example:

    # only the 10.0.0.0/8 network may reach the SSH and direct ports of dev environments
iptables -I DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m multiport --dports 2200:2399 ! -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j DROP

  • Port 8002 needs nothing when SlotServe runs in Docker: the gateway lives inside SlotServe's container and is reached as slotserve-gw on each environment's network. When SlotServe runs directly on the host, it listens on Docker's bridge address (docker0); a host firewall that drops traffic from containers to the host must allow TCP 8002 from Docker's networks (by default inside 172.16.0.0/12 and 192.168.0.0/16), for example ufw allow from 172.16.0.0/12 to any port 8002 proto tcp.

  • Behind a reverse proxy, 8000 and 8001 can be bound to 127.0.0.1 (ports: - "127.0.0.1:8000:8000") so that only the proxy reaches them.

docs.title: Forgotten admin password or locked out
docs.text:
Symptom. An admin cannot sign in; or "too many attempts".

Diagnose. Failed sign-ins lock an account for 15 minutes from the address they came from (10 failures per account and address, 30 per address); other addresses are not affected. Behind a proxy without SLOTSERVE_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, everyone shares one address (Reverse proxy).

Fix.

  • Another admin resets the password in Admin → Users.

  • On the server:

    docker compose exec slotserve slotserve reset-password <username>    # asks for the new password
docker compose exec slotserve slotserve set-admin <username>         # if no admin is left

    The reset signs that account out everywhere. The lock is held in memory: docker compose restart slotserve clears it. - No admin account at all any more: setup code.

Prevent. Two admins; passwords in a password manager.

docs.title: Disk full
docs.text:
Symptom. The health check disk warns or errors; backups, downloads or model loads fail with "No space left on device"; the database cannot be written.

Diagnose.

df -h                                  # which file system
du -sh data/* | sort -h | tail         # SlotServe's data directory
docker system df                       # images, containers, volumes, build cache
du -sh "$MODELS_DIR"

Usual culprits: models, Docker images (environment templates, saved images, kept environments' snapshots), /workspace volumes, old backups and upgrade snapshots in data/backups/, logs.

Fix.

  • Models no one uses: delete them in Models (removes the file).
  • Docker: docker image prune (unused images), and saved environment images people no longer need (deleting the saved template removes its image). Do not docker volume prune blindly: volumes hold people's /workspace.
  • Backups: upgrade snapshots and prerestore bundles are never removed automatically; delete old ones by hand once you no longer need them. Lower backup_keep if needed.
  • Logs: model server logs rotate at 20 MB, the SlotServe container's Docker log at 5 × 50 MB. Containers of dev environments are limited the same way.
  • Usage records are folded after SLOTSERVE_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS; the audit log is kept for SLOTSERVE_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS.

Prevent. Models and Docker's data root on a different disk than the system; a backup target; set a soft limit on personal storages; watch the disk check's warning (it starts at twice the download free-space minimum, at least 5 GB).

docs.title: Dev environment does not start
docs.text:
Symptom. An environment's card says it did not start; the person was notified.

Diagnose. As admin, Dev environments → Everyone, open the environment: its error and Logs. Recognised errors come with a diagnosis (cause and next steps); see FAQ: diagnoses. Then by cause:

Cause Typical error Fix Image pull pull access denied, manifest unknown, toomanyrequests Check the image name and tag; the Docker host's access to the registry (proxy, mirror); docker login on the host for private images or Docker Hub limits; pull it once by hand. Port conflict port is already allocated, address already in use Something else on the host uses a port of the SSH or direct range: move the range (settings) or the other program. Mounts failed to mount local volume, mount error(13), access denied by server Storage: Check it in Admin → Storage; install nfs-common / cifs-utils on the Docker host; NFS exports must allow the host. Storage directory: must be a path on the Docker host. CPU set Requested CPUs are not available, cpuset Fewer cores than lanes reserve: lower CPU cores reserved per GPU; after a CPU change restart SlotServe so it reads the host again. GPU could not select device driver "nvidia" GPUs gone Lane without GPUs devenv_lane_no_gpus Give the lane its GPUs in Admin → GPUs & lanes. Docker Cannot connect to the Docker daemon Docker running? Socket mounted? See Dev environments: Docker.

Fix. Fix the cause, then Try again on the environment.

Prevent. Run python -m tools.verify after changes to Docker, drivers or templates (Verify); prefer images from registries you control for important templates.

docs.title: GPUs gone after a driver or Docker upgrade
docs.text:
Symptom. The health check gpu says "No GPU detected"; models fail with CUDA errors; dev environments fail with could not select device driver "nvidia".

Diagnose.

nvidia-smi                                                  # on the host: does the driver work?
docker run --rm --gpus all ubuntu nvidia-smi                # can Docker give containers a GPU?
docker compose exec slotserve nvidia-smi                    # does SlotServe's container see them?

Fix.

  • nvidia-smi fails on the host: the kernel module does not match the new driver; reboot, or reinstall the driver for the running kernel.

  • Only Docker fails: reconfigure the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and restart Docker:

    sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
sudo systemctl restart docker

  • Models fail with "CUDA driver version is insufficient": the engine needs a newer driver, or rebuild it for the installed CUDA; with Docker the CUDA major of CUDA_IMAGE must match your llama-server build.

  • Then docker compose up -d (a Docker restart stops SlotServe unless restart: unless-stopped brings it back).

Prevent. Pin the driver packages (apt-mark hold), upgrade drivers and Docker in a maintenance window, and run slotserve doctor and tools/verify afterwards.

docs.title: Suspected account or key leak
docs.text:
Symptom. Unknown sign-ins, API usage nobody recognises, a key or password posted somewhere.

Diagnose.

  • Admin → Audit log: filter by the person, by action (auth.* for sign-ins and failed sign-ins, key.* for API keys) and dates; addresses are recorded (see Reverse proxy for real addresses). Export the selection as CSV for the record.
  • Admin → Request log: requests by person, key and source (API key, environment key, Playground); each API key shows the address it was last used from.

Fix.

  1. Disable the account (Admin → Users) if it is compromised: it is signed out everywhere and its bookings end.
  2. Revoke API keys (Admin → API keys, or the person under Access credentials). Environment keys end with their environment.
  3. Sign out everywhere: the person uses Settings → Signed-in devices → Sign out all other devices; a password change or an admin's reset does the same.
  4. Remove SSH keys the person does not recognise (Access credentials) and set a new environment password.
  5. If an admin account or the server's .env leaked, also rotate the secret key and change the invite code, chat platform tokens and SLOTSERVE_METRICS_TOKEN.

Prevent. Keys with an expiry, invite links instead of a shared invite code, few admins, and review the audit log now and then.

docs.title: Verify on real hardware
docs.text:
tools/verify checks a running installation end to end, through its public API, the way people use it: a GPU booking and an OpenAI-style request, every built-in dev environment template with SSH (key and password) and its web interface, an environment without GPU, a storage, the container hardening and the security protections. It creates a throw-away account and removes it again; it changes no settings (a feature that is off is reported as skipped). Run it after installing, after upgrades of SlotServe, drivers or Docker, and for every release candidate.

From a checkout of the SlotServe repository on a machine that reaches the server (Python 3.11+ with httpx, an OpenSSH client; sshpass for the password logins):

python -m tools.verify --url http://gpu-server:8000 --admin <admin account> --out reports/

The admin password is asked for (or SLOTSERVE_VERIFY_PASSWORD). Useful options: --lane, --model, --templates pytorch,vscode (a subset), --storage-id or --storage-host-path, --no-ssh, --no-web, --save-image, --destructive (also a fork bomb in an environment without GPU), --keep (keep the test account for debugging), --insecure (self-signed TLS). Pulling every template image takes a while the first time.

It writes verify-report-<host>-<version>.md and .json. Results are pass, fail, skip (a feature is off or a tool is missing), pending or manual: the manual ones are browser checks the tool cannot do (a CSRF proof-of-concept page written next to the report, and the isolation of two environments' web pages), with instructions in the report. Exit code 0 means nothing failed, 1 that a check failed, 2 that the server could not be reached or signed in to. Attach the report to the release pull request (see the release checklist).

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text: The release owner (a maintainer) goes through this list for every minor release. Patch releases skip the release candidate when they only contain fixes that were verified on their own. Tick the boxes in the release pull request.

docs.title: Image tags
docs.text:
Tag pushed Images published GitHub release vX.Y.Z X.Y.Z, X.Y, latest release, notes from the X.Y.Z section of CHANGELOG.md vX.Y.Z-rc1 (anything with a -) X.Y.Z-rc1, rc pre-release, notes from [Unreleased] plus changes/unreleased/

A pre-release never moves latest or X.Y. docker-compose.yml follows a minor version (slotserve:X.Y), so existing installations only pick up final releases of their minor.

To check the tag rules without publishing anything, run the Release workflow by hand (Actions → Release → Run workflow) with a tag such as v0.0.0-test: it prints and checks the image tags and the notes, and builds, pushes and releases nothing.

docs.title: 1. Before the release candidate
docs.text:
• [ ] Every change of the release has a fragment in changes/unreleased/ or an entry under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md; python tools/release_notes.py check passes and preview reads well.
  • [ ] Changed behaviour of existing installations is listed under Breaking changes, with what to do.
  • [ ] CI is green on main (lint, backend, frontend, end-to-end, docs, Docker image).
  • [ ] Database migrations of the release are tested against a copy of the previous release's data directory.
  • [ ] The minor version in docker-compose.yml and the docs is the one being released.
  • [ ] The docs are current: mkdocs build --strict passes, backend/tests/test_docs_anchors.py passes, the operations runbooks cover every new setting an admin must know, and the upgrade section lists what people will notice.
  • [ ] Security review of what the release adds (see Security review below), signed off in the release pull request.

docs.title: 2. Release candidate
docs.text:
• [ ] Bump the version in backend/pyproject.toml, backend/slotserve/__init__.py and frontend/package.json to X.Y.Z (the candidate is tagged on that commit).
  • [ ] git tag vX.Y.Z-rc1 && git push origin vX.Y.Z-rc1; the workflow publishes X.Y.Z-rc1 and rc.
  • [ ] Verification on real hardware with python -m tools.verify across the verification matrix; every report (verify-report-<host>-<version>.md) is attached to the release pull request, with the manual checks filled in and every failure turned into an issue.
  • [ ] Upgrade, backup and restore rehearsed on a copy of real data.
  • [ ] The candidate runs on at least one real installation for 3 days or more without new problems. Each fix gets a new candidate (-rc2, ...).

docs.title: 3. Release
docs.text:
• [ ] python tools/release_notes.py release X.Y.Z (moves [Unreleased] and the fragments under ## [X.Y.Z] - <today> and deletes the fragments); review CHANGELOG.md.
  • [ ] Commit (Release X.Y.Z), then git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin main vX.Y.Z.
  • [ ] The workflow publishes X.Y.Z, X.Y and latest and creates the GitHub release; check the release page and docker pull ghcr.io/peleryuan/slotserve:X.Y.

docs.title: 4. After the release
docs.text:
• [ ] The documentation site shows the new version's docs.
  • [ ] Announce the release with its breaking changes: the GitHub release page (its notes come from the changelog) links the upgrade runbook; point the issue tracker's pinned discussion or the project's chat group at it.
  • [ ] Open the next [Unreleased] work; problems found after the release become X.Y.(Z+1) fixes.

docs.title: Security review
docs.text:
Before the first release candidate, a maintainer who did not write the change goes through what the release adds and checks each item with a proof of concept against a running installation (most are also covered by tests; the point is to see them fail on a real browser and a real Docker host):

  • [ ] New write endpoints are covered by the CSRF test generated from the routes; in a browser, the CSRF page written by tools/verify changes nothing from another origin, from a direct port or from the web port.
  • [ ] Sign-in: a cookie signed with the old default key is refused; the first admin needs the setup code; throttling locks per account and address; changing a password signs out other sessions.
  • [ ] Credentials: new kinds of keys are scoped and expire; no secret appears in logs, the audit log, doctor --json, /api/health evidence or a saved image (docker inspect, docker history).
  • [ ] Container fields: every new field of the container spec is in the golden spec tests and reviewed; no new privilege, capability, host namespace, device or bind mount outside the allowed folders; hardening holds (no-new-privileges, dropped capabilities, process and memory limits).
  • [ ] Published ports: every port the release opens is in Ports and firewall, is behind the SlotServe login or needs an explicit confirmation, and dev environment pages cannot act in SlotServe or in another environment (the web origin checks of tools/verify).
  • [ ] Root-equivalent settings (engine commands, mounted folders, images) ask for the password again and are announced to all admins.

docs.title: Verification matrix
docs.text:
Run tools/verify (see Verify on real hardware) on enough installations to cover:

Dimension Cover Machines A Linux machine with an NVIDIA GPU; a machine without GPU Deployment Docker Compose with the published candidate image; without Docker Dev environments Every built-in template booked with a GPU, without GPU, kept and continued, saved as an image; a shared idle environment Logins SSH key, environment password, web interfaces through a reverse proxy with HTTPS Storage Host folder, NFS, SMB Engines llama.cpp; vLLM Notifications Telegram and one other chat platform; the inbox Browsers Chrome, Firefox, Safari Failures Out of memory in an environment, a fork bomb (--destructive), Docker restarted, host rebooted, disk nearly full: the health table and the alerts tell the truth, and SlotServe recovers

Each report records the host, versions (SlotServe, driver, Docker) and the results; the manual browser checks are ticked in the report by the person who ran them.

docs.title: Upgrade, backup and restore rehearsal
docs.text:
• [ ] A copy of a real data directory of the previous release starts on the candidate: snapshot taken, migration report clean, the health table as expected; then roll back to the snapshot with the previous image and upgrade again (Roll back).
  • [ ] The daily bundle is copied to a backup target on another machine (a NAS path and a managed storage).
  • [ ] A bundle is restored on another machine with slotserve restore; the reconciliation report matches what really happened.
  • [ ] An admin who did not write the runbooks resets an admin password and restores from a backup using only Operations; every point where they got stuck is fixed in the docs.

docs.title: How scheduling works
docs.text: Each lane (a group of GPUs; a single-GPU host has one) runs exactly one model server process. Every few seconds - and immediately after a booking or model change - the lane's scheduler decides which model should be loaded and moves the process towards it. Lanes are scheduled independently.

docs.title: Choosing the target model
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    tick(["Every few seconds, for each lane"]) --> now{"Booking in progress?"}
    now -- "Yes, run a model" --> booked["Booked model and preset"]
    now -- "Yes, whole GPU" --> stop["Stop the model server"]
    now -- "No" --> soon{"Next booking starts within<br/>its load time + 60 s<br/>or the minimum preload time?"}
    soon -- "Yes" --> preload["Preload the next booking's model"]
    soon -- "No" --> gap{"Gap too short to be<br/>worth loading the default?"}
    gap -- "Yes" --> preload
    gap -- "No" --> manual{"Admin chose a model<br/>or unload manually?"}
    manual -- "Yes" --> choice["The admin's choice"]
    manual -- "No" --> default["The lane's default model<br/>(or nothing)"]

In detail:

  1. A booking is in progress → that booking's model and preset. For a whole GPU booking: nothing (the model server is stopped).
  2. The next booking starts within its model's estimated load time + 60 s, or within the minimum preload time (3 minutes by default), whichever is earlier → preload the next booking's model now. Before a whole-GPU booking, the model server is stopped SLOTSERVE_STOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS + 60 s early.
  3. The next booking is so close that loading the default model would only be usable briefly (gap < default load + next load + 2 × buffer) → skip the default and load the next booking's model directly.
  4. An admin chose a model (or unloading) manually → that, until its time is up or the next booking starts.
  5. Otherwise → the lane's default model (or nothing, if no default is set).

A model plus a preset counts as one target: switching presets of the same file reloads the model server.

The process is only restarted when the target differs from what is loaded. Releasing a booking early triggers an immediate re-evaluation.

docs.title: Load time estimates
docs.text:
• After a model has loaded at least once, its estimate is the average of its last five successful loads.
  • Before that, it is file size ÷ SLOTSERVE_DISK_READ_MBPS + 15 s.

Loads from spinning disks are slow and the page cache only helps when the host has more free RAM than the model's size. Keeping frequently used models on an SSD is the single biggest improvement.

docs.title: Who may call the API
docs.text:
Situation Booking owner Everyone else Lane not booked allowed (current model) allowed (current model) Booking active, its model ready allowed 403 gpu_reserved Booking active, its model still loading 503 + Retry-After 403 gpu_reserved Whole-GPU booking active 503 gpu_exclusive 403 gpu_reserved

A booking that is still awaiting approval does not make the lane busy and loads nothing; it only keeps others from booking the same time. With several lanes, see which lane serves a request.

Free use of the idle GPU is best-effort: it may be interrupted when the next booking's model is preloaded.

docs.title: Back-to-back bookings
docs.text: Loading can only start after the previous booking ends. If two adjacent bookings use different models, the second booking spends the start of its slot loading. When both use the same model there is no reload at all. The booking dialog points this out.

docs.title: Switching without cutting requests off
docs.text:
When the target model changes, SlotServe first lets requests that are already running finish (up to SLOTSERVE_DRAIN_SECONDS, 30 s by default). Meanwhile new requests get 503 model_switching with a Retry-After header. Then the model server is stopped and the next model loads. Reload model restarts immediately.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Clients
    participant G as Gateway
    participant S as Scheduler
    participant M as Model server
    S->>G: target changes
    Note over G,M: drain: running requests finish (up to DRAIN_SECONDS)
    C->>G: new request
    G-->>C: 503 model_switching + Retry-After
    S->>M: stop, then start the next model
    M-->>S: /health returns 200
    C->>G: request
    G->>M: forward
    M-->>C: response (streamed)

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
• If the log shows that the GPU ran out of memory, the error says so and suggests lowering -ngl or -c. Models whose file is larger than the GPU's memory are marked Larger than GPU memory in the model list and the booking dialog.

  • If the model server exits or does not become healthy within SLOTSERVE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, the runtime is marked failed with the reason, and the scheduler retries with a growing back-off (30 s → 10 min).

  • Fallback: while a booked model is waiting for its next retry, the default model serves the booking so the booker is not left without a model. The overview shows a banner, and the booker and admins are notified. When the retry succeeds, the booked model takes over again.
  • The overview page shows the error, and Server log shows the model server's own output.
  • The flags SlotServe sets itself (for llama.cpp -m, --host, --port and --alias; for vLLM and SGLang the model, host, port and served name) are stripped from user arguments, so a typo there cannot break routing.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Admins add the storage dev environments get in Admin → Storage: a directory on the Docker host, an NFS export or an SMB/CIFS share. Each storage has a purpose, says who gets it and is checked regularly.

Without any storage nothing changes: /workspace and kept directories live in Docker named volumes (or under the legacy Storage directory setting, see Dev environments).

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Type What you enter How containers get it Host directory An absolute path on the machine Docker runs on, e.g. /srv/data A bind mount NFS Server (host name or IP), export path (/export/data), optional mount options (default nfsvers=4) A Docker named volume of the local driver with type=nfs SMB / CIFS Server, share (share or share/folder; //server/share/folder can be pasted as a whole), user name and password, optional mount options (default vers=3.0) A Docker named volume of the local driver with type=cifs

NFS and SMB are mounted by Docker itself when a container starts, so there is nothing to put in /etc/fstab and the same storage can later be used on other machines. The Docker host only needs the usual mount helpers:

  • NFS: nfs-common (Debian, Ubuntu) or nfs-utils (RHEL, Fedora, openSUSE);
  • SMB: cifs-utils.

Docker Desktop, rootless Docker and Podman may not be able to mount NFS or SMB volumes; use a host directory there (mounted on the host by other means) instead.

The SMB password is stored encrypted with SLOTSERVE_SECRET_KEY and never shown again (leave the field empty to keep it). Docker needs it in the volume's options, so anyone who can run docker volume inspect on the host can read it - give SlotServe a share account of its own. Because mount options are one comma-separated list, the password cannot contain commas. Mount options cannot contain addr, username or password, which SlotServe sets itself.

docs.title: Purposes
docs.text:
Purpose In environments On the storage Shared data At its mount path (e.g. /data/team), read-only if ticked The whole storage Personal spaces Each person's folder is their /workspace, instead of a Docker volume users/u<user id> Project data The kept directories of kept environments and templates projects/p<project id>/<path>, templates/u<user id>-t<template id>/<path> Model library At its mount path if one is set (e.g. /mnt/models/team), usually read-only Model files
  • A person's folder (and every kept directory) is created the first time it is needed and filled from the image, like a new Docker volume. A short-lived helper container of SLOTSERVE_STORAGE_HELPER_IMAGE does that (never the environment's own image; the image's content is copied out with Docker's archive API), so SlotServe itself needs no access to the storage. For a host directory the helper mounts only the parent folder it works in; an NFS export or SMB share is mounted from its root, since a folder that does not exist yet cannot be mounted.
  • Shared idle environments (see Dev environments) get every storage open to everyone, and the personal storage as a whole at /workspaces: each person's folder /workspaces/u<user id> belongs to their account there and is only open to them. Files written as root in a booked environment may need a chown to be changed from a shared environment.
  • Project data takes over from the Storage directory setting for kept directories; with neither, Docker volumes are used. The setting still decides where the homes of shared environments are kept.
  • Model library: SlotServe scans it for GGUF files (Models → Scan folder) and it can be picked as the target of a download (storage_id in POST /api/downloads and POST /api/downloads/hf). SlotServe reads and writes it at the path SlotServe reads it at: for a host directory that defaults to the directory itself (when SlotServe runs on the host). For NFS or SMB, mount the share on the SlotServe machine (or into the SlotServe container) and enter that path. SLOTSERVE_MODELS_DIR stays the default library and is still mounted at /models.
  • When several storages have the same purpose, a person gets the first one (the oldest) they may use for personal spaces and project data, and all of them for shared data and model libraries.

docs.title: Who gets it
docs.text:
Everyone, chosen people or admins only. People who may not use a storage do not get it mounted; for personal spaces and project data they fall back to the next storage or to Docker volumes. On Dev environments everyone sees the storages their environments get, where they are mounted and their own usage.

Mount paths must be absolute and cannot be system directories, /workspace, /workspaces, /models or overlap another storage's mount path.

docs.title: Checks, usage and soft limits
docs.text:
Check mounts the storage in a short-lived container of SLOTSERVE_STORAGE_HELPER_IMAGE (default busybox:1.37, pulled when missing) and shows whether it is reachable, the error if not, free and total space (df) and whether it is writable. For personal spaces it also measures every person's folder (du); Usage lists them, largest first.

SlotServe checks every storage on its own every SLOTSERVE_STORAGE_CHECK_MINUTES (default 30; 0 = only when an admin clicks Check) while dev environments are on. Admins are notified when a storage that worked stops working.

A personal storage can have a soft limit per person: people above it get a notification (and admins one too), once until they are back under it. Nothing is blocked.

docs.title: Changing or removing a storage
docs.text:
Changes apply to containers started afterwards. Kept environments compare the storages they were created with: if they differ at the next booking, the container is snapshotted and recreated with the new mounts (installed software is kept). Changing how an NFS/SMB storage is mounted creates new Docker volumes; the old ones are removed once no container uses them.

Removing a storage only removes it from SlotServe; the data on it stays. Deleting a kept environment with its data also removes its folder on the project storage.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
NFS server (Linux), exporting /srv/nfs/homes to the Docker host 10.0.0.20:

sudo apt install nfs-kernel-server
sudo mkdir -p /srv/nfs/homes
echo '/srv/nfs/homes 10.0.0.20(rw,sync,no_subtree_check,no_root_squash)' | sudo tee -a /etc/exports
sudo exportfs -ra

no_root_squash lets the helper create folders and set their owner. In SlotServe: type NFS, server 10.0.0.15, export path /srv/nfs/homes, purpose Personal spaces. For NFSv3 use the options nfsvers=3,nolock.

SMB share on a NAS or a Samba server ([team] with path = /srv/samba/team, a user slotserve created with smbpasswd -a slotserve): type SMB / CIFS, server nas.local, share team (or team/datasets), user slotserve and its password, purpose Shared data, mount path /data/team, Read-only. CIFS has no Unix owners: files belong to root in the container unless you add e.g. uid=0,gid=0,file_mode=0660,dir_mode=0770 (or 0777 for shared idle environments, whose accounts are not root). Other useful options: vers=2.1 for older servers, domain=STUDIO.

To try a storage from the Docker host by hand:

docker volume create --driver local --opt type=nfs --opt o=addr=10.0.0.15,nfsvers=4 --opt device=:/srv/nfs/homes test-nfs
docker run --rm -v test-nfs:/s busybox:1.37 df -h /s
docker volume rm test-nfs

docs.title: Booking the GPU
docs.text:
Open Schedule and drag across the calendar, or press New booking. Choose what to book, adjust the time and add an optional note.

  • Bookings snap to 30-minute slots (configurable) and cannot overlap.
  • A slot that has already started can still be booked; it starts now. Start now in the dialog does this for you.
  • The dialog shows the model's estimated load time. If someone else's booking ends exactly when yours starts and uses a different model, loading happens inside your slot and the dialog warns you.
  • During your booking only your API keys are accepted.
  • Cancel an upcoming booking, or End now to release the GPU early. The default model comes back right away.

docs.title: Booking types
docs.text: Type What happens during the slot Run a model Your model (optionally with one of its presets) is loaded before the slot starts. Only your API keys are accepted. Whole GPU The model server is stopped shortly before the slot, so the GPU is completely free for training or any other program. The API returns 503 gpu_exclusive. The default model comes back when the slot ends. Dev environment A Docker container with the GPU and SSH runs for the slot; your /workspace is kept. See Dev environments.

docs.title: Changing bookings
docs.text:
• Edit an upcoming booking to move it or change its model, preset or note.
  • Extend a running booking by 30 minutes, 1 hour or 2 hours, if the time after it is free. You can also shorten it with Edit.
  • Repeat weekly creates the same slot for several weeks. Either every week fits, or nothing is booked and the dialog says which week clashes. Cancelling one booking of a series asks whether to cancel only that one or the rest of the series as well.
  • Admins can edit or cancel anyone's booking and book for someone else. The person is notified on the chat platforms they linked.

docs.title: Waitlist
docs.text: If the time you want is taken, the dialog offers Join waitlist. When that time frees up (a cancellation or an early end), SlotServe books it for you automatically, or just notifies you if you unticked Book automatically. Your open waitlist entries appear under My bookings.

docs.title: Lanes and approval
docs.text: With several GPU groups ("lanes"), the calendar shows a tab per lane and the booking dialog asks which lane to book. When approval mode is on, the dialog says if your booking needs an admin's approval; it then shows as Awaiting approval and you are notified of the decision. See GPUs, lanes & engines.

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text: Admins can limit how many hours one person may book per calendar week and how many open bookings they may hold. The limits do not apply to admins.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Models lists every registered model with its engine, size, estimated load time and launch arguments.

  • Scan folder registers new .gguf files from the models directory as llama.cpp models.
  • Add model registers a model by hand: pick the engine (llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang or custom) and give a file, directory or Hugging Face repository.
  • Edit changes the name (the model id clients see), launch arguments and description. The person who added a model and admins can edit or delete it.
